General interface to reconstructing rounded numbers

Source: R/reround.R
reround.Rd

reround() rounds a vector of reconstructed values the way they are assumed to have been rounded originally. It is the common interface to all of roundwork's rounding functions and to base::round().

Usage

reround(
  x,
  digits = 0L,
  rounding = "up_or_down",
  threshold = 5,
  symmetric = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Numeric. Values to round.

digits

Integer. Number of decimal places to round to, i.e., the number in the reported values. Length 1 or the length of x. Must be whole numbers; a missing value propagates to a missing result.

rounding

String (length 1). The rounding method. Default is "up_or_down", which returns two values per element of x: rounded up and rounded down.

threshold

Numeric (length 1). For "up_from", "down_from", and "up_from_or_down_from", the point within a step at which rounding switches direction, in tenths of a step; greater than 0 and less than 10. Default is 5, which makes these methods the same as "up", "down", and "up_or_down". See round_up_from().

symmetric

Logical (length 1). If TRUE, negative numbers are rounded like their absolute values under "up", "down", "up_or_down", and the "*_from" methods. Default is FALSE. Must not be TRUE with a "ties_*" method, which already fixes the direction: "ties_up" with symmetric = TRUE would be "ties_away", so write that instead.

Value

Numeric. One value per element of x, except for the compound methods "up_or_down", "up_from_or_down_from", and "ceiling_or_floor", which return two: the results of their two constituent procedures, next to each other, as c(up_1, down_1, up_2, down_2, ...). Each pair belongs to one element of x, so the pairs must not be pooled across elements.

Details

reround() calls the rounding function that rounding names. See vignette("rounding-options") for the possible values, and round_up() and round_ceiling() for the functions themselves.
